chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Mudabbir (slave manumitted upon the master's death), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is in the status of the bequest; he returns in it and in whatever he desires from it.'

key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرِ: A slave manumitted upon the owner's death
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: He has the right to retract or alter

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a Mudabbir in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a Mudabbir holds a status analogous to a beneficiary of a bequest (wasiyyah), granting the owner the discretion to emancipate the slave fully or partially at any time before death. This ruling underscores the flexibility in manumission practices within Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing the Mudabbir from other categories of slaves by linking their freedom to the owner's volition similar to testamentary gifts. The hadith highlights the charitable and liberating spirit encouraged in Islamic law regarding the gradual or immediate freeing of slaves.
